A theme is a folder. yapmod looks for `manifest.json` in that folder, reads the stylesheet it names, and stores the result as a bundle. Only `id` and `name` are required.

## Complete example

```json
{
  "id": "midnight-blurple",
  "name": "Midnight Blurple",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "author": "Your name",
  "description": "Cool blues on a deep navy base.",
  "license": "MIT",
  "mode": "both",
  "tags": ["dark", "blue"],
  "api": 1,
  "preview": "preview.png",
  "css": "theme.css"
}
```

```text
midnight-blurple/
├── manifest.json
├── theme.css
└── preview.png
```

## Top-level fields

| Field | Required | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | Yes | string | The identity of the theme. It becomes the installed folder name and the value of `data-yapmod-theme`. |
| `name` | Yes | string | Shown in the gallery. Up to 120 characters, and it cannot be blank. |
| `version` | No | string | The version of the theme itself. |
| `author` | No | string | Who made it. |
| `description` | No | string | A short line shown with the theme. |
| `license` | No | string | The license of the theme. |
| `mode` | No | `"dark"` \| `"light"` \| `"both"` | Defaults to `dark`. Unknown values are also treated as `dark`. |
| `tags` | No | string[] | Search words used by the Community gallery. |
| `api` | No | number | The theme format the theme was written against. The current value is `1`. |
| `preview` | No | string | File name of a preview image inside the theme folder. |
| `css` | No | string | File name of the stylesheet. Defaults to `theme.css`. |

The generated type mirrors what the app deserializes:

<ApiType name="ThemeManifest" source="theme" members={false} />

## Files and names

- The manifest must be valid JSON.
- `id` must be non-empty, must not start with `.`, and may use letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`. Because it becomes a folder name, keep it short and stable.
- `css` and `preview` must name a file directly inside the theme folder. The name cannot start with `.`, cannot contain `/` or `\`, and cannot contain `..`.
- The stylesheet must exist. If `css` is omitted, yapmod looks for `theme.css`.
- `preview` is optional. It is read only from the extension allowlist below; an unsupported format is ignored rather than breaking the install.
- Importing copies the whole folder, including extra files. Symbolic links are rejected, so a theme cannot point outside itself.
- A theme with an `api` newer than the app understands is refused instead of being applied halfway.

## Limits

<Limits kind="theme" />

## Mode

`mode` answers one question: does the theme have its own opinion about dark and light?

| Value | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `dark` | The theme is always shown in dark mode. |
| `light` | The theme is always shown in light mode. |
| `both` | The theme follows the app's **Mode** setting, which can follow the system. |

`dark` is the default, including for an unknown value, because a theme written before modes existed was almost certainly a dark theme. A one-mode theme still receives `data-yapmod-mode` so the same stylesheet can be reused unchanged.

## Local and Community differences

The app is deliberately forgiving with a local theme and strict with the published catalog:

| Check | Local import | Community build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unknown manifest fields | Ignored | Rejected |
| `id` characters | Letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.`; any length | Letters, digits, `-`, `_`; must start with a letter or digit; at most 24 characters |
| Folder name | Does not have to match `id` | Must match `id` |
| `mode` | Unknown values fall back to `dark` | Must be `dark`, `light` or `both` |
| `tags` | Not limited by the app | At most 20, each at most 32 characters |
| CSS | Applied as written | `@import`, `behavior:` and backslash escapes rejected |
| Size | Read from disk | Enforced at the [limits](#limits) above |

The Community build also defaults a missing `mode` to `both` and a missing `api` to `1`, and it rejects an `api` newer than the catalog supports. Match the published rules even for a local theme if you intend to submit it later.

## What the app stores

After installation the app builds a bundle from the manifest. Only these values reach the client:

<ApiType name="ThemeBundle" source="theme" members={false} />

The stylesheet text and preview data URI are included. Fields the manifest does not use are not passed on, and the bundle has no script, module or executable entry point.
